After weeks of only having weekly usage caps, OpenAI today announced it will restore the 5-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus subscribers. Here are the details.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers restored to 5-hour usage cap

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, Head of Codex and ChatGPT Engineering at OpenAI, announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), Plus subscribers will once again have a 5-hour usage limit on Codex and ChatGPT Work.

When users hit the 5-hour or weekly usage cap, they can wait for the next cycle to reset, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI also occasionally resets users' usage caps for free, while stored reset counts can be obtained through specific promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, in recent weeks, OpenAI temporarily removed the 5-hour usage limit on Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly cap.

During this period, the company also reset users' weekly usage early several times to celebrate milestones reached, including hitting an additional one million active users across the two (now merged) platforms.

However, Tibo explained tonight on X:

Tomorrow we are restoring the 5-hour usage limit on Plus accounts for ChatGPT Work and Codex. I mentioned this earlier but then postponed it. This is necessary because (a) the 5-hour limit helps us distribute compute load evenly, allowing the weekly usage allowance to remain generous; and (b) Plus plan users are mostly lighter or newer users, but they often inadvertently burn through the entire week's allowance and then feel confused, which isn't a great experience. For the next few months, the 5-hour limit will not be enabled on the Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscription plans.

Tibo made no mention of any changes to Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently use a separate credits-based usage system.

Will the restoration of the 5-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
